votes.s: 226 Kane Street (Kane Street Synagogue): Certificate of Appropriateness approved with the condition that lights are shielded to prevent light spillage onto Kane Street
votes.f: David Briggs presented a motion to approve with conditions an application for a Certificate of Appropriateness at the Kane Street Synagogue for a rooftop enclosure of mechanical equipment, modification of the sanctuary window, and new courtyard lighting. Mandi asked whether the board could also request sidewalk repairs as part of the project; Eric explained that the sidewalk condition is not within the board’s purview, but that CB6 could reach out to the applicant with the request. Donna McGill of the Cobble Hill Association asked about the lighting and possible spillover onto the street. David explained that the lights are intended to illuminate the stained glass in the sanctuary when it is in use and not at other times, and that because of the risk of spillover the committee asked the applicant to install snoots on the fixtures to focus light only on the windows. The condition for approval was that "lights are shielded to prevent light spillage onto Kane Street." There was no quorum in committee. The motion was approved by the board unanimously.

votes.s: 226 Kane Street (Kane Street Synagogue): Certificate of Appropriateness for a rooftop alteration and primary facade window in the Cobble Hill Historic District
votes.f: Motion by Jerry Armer, seconded by Maddie Murphy, to conditionally approve with shielding of lights to prevent spillage of light onto Kane Street. The application, presented by Tal Schori of GRT Architects, comprises an acoustic enclosure for rooftop HVAC equipment, a new pergola with horizontal covering and a fine mesh fence replacing the existing chain link fence, new LED lighting in the courtyard, and modifications of the existing sanctuary window. Committee comments concerned illumination levels, pergola color, the rating of the acoustic enclosure and the extent of window restoration; the synagogue affirmed an off-white pergola and that light fixtures will project only on east sanctuary windows and only when the sanctuary is in use. The Cobble Hill Association had no comments. Motion informally passed unanimously.

votes.s: Hamilton Avenue: DOT changes approved, with further study of the street direction changes with neighborhood residents
votes.f: Tony Melone presented the motion to approve all changes presented by DOT on both sides of Hamilton Avenue, with the addition of HAWK signals at the midblock crossings, intended to resolve speeding, weaving and a lack of pedestrian crossings. DOT proposed street direction changes for Woodhull and Rapelye Streets, new crosswalks across Hamilton Avenue, lane reductions on Hamilton Avenue and Woodhull Street, and delineators to prevent illegal right turns. Approved in committee with quorum. Board member Josh Pacheco, who lives in the affected area, raised community concerns that the direction changes would make legal truck turns difficult and could block access to a gas station, while supporting the midblock crosswalks. Jerry Armer offered a friendly amendment asking DOT to reconsider the street direction changes and hear community feedback. The motion, modified to approve the DOT changes with further study of the street direction changes with the participation of neighborhood residents, passed unanimously.

votes.s: 184 Lincoln Place: motion to disapprove a Certificate of Appropriateness for a rooftop extension in the Park Slope Historic District
votes.f: Kathleen Addison presented a motion to disapprove an application for a Certificate of Appropriateness for a rooftop extension at 184 Lincoln Place, in the Park Slope Historic District. Community members had voiced concerns about the visibility of the extension from Berkeley Place, and the committee considered the design to lack historic character, due in part to stucco that does not match the character of the area. The committee voted unanimously to disapprove, with quorum. The motion was approved by the board, with Katie Bishop opposed and Tony Melone and Max Bernstein abstaining.

votes.f: II. Chairperson’s Report Chairperson Eric McClure thanked the Van Alen Institute for hosting our meetings and noted that their ability to host hybrid meetings is a great asset to the board. He welcomed newly appointed board members to their first meeting as members and noted that Community Board service is an important way to get involved in the community. He announced that the Carroll Street Bridge will reopen on June 15th, with use limited to pedestrians, bikes, and emergency vehicles, in keeping with the motion previously passed by the Board. He noted that the bridge is one of only four retractile drawbridges in the United States and that limiting vehicle use will help sustain the bridge’s condition in the future.

The job description was reviewed, edited, and approved by the Executive Committee at its November meeting.To approve the job description for the District Manager position. Discussion ensued, with various Board Members asking about the process of by which the Finance, Personnel, and Law committee drafted the description. Some questions about language were asked, and some Board Members suggested various alternatives to certain terms, particularly in the first three paragraphs of the description. Two friendly amendments were accepted: changing the first sentence from “This is a management class position” to “This is an at-will management class position” and the second sentence in the first numbered job responsibility, Supervision of Staff/District Office, from “The District Office processes inquiries…” to “The District Office processes and responds to inquiries…”.

Presentation by Chris Hrones, DOT on the milling/paving program. All roadways are rated on scale of 1 – 10 every 2 years. 10 is the best. 7 may trigger a repaving. 5 – 6 is a definite repaving. Community board input can help address priorities. DOT now going to each community board every year to discuss repaving needs. Used to be every 18 months. Street volumes also determine priority. Larger arterials may be prioritized over smaller side streets.Proposed by Matthew Silverman ...that DOT prioritize streets with bike lanes over other streets with comparable conditions. Seconded by Eric McClure. Discussion. Motion withdrawn. Suggestion to modify language to include all “vulnerable street users.” MOTION: Proposed by Jerry Armer “In evaluating streets to prioritize for milling and repaving, DOT consider safety of vulnerable street users.” Question called.

votes.f: ay.” Sara Weinbrom presented to the committee the proposal to co-name Fifth Street between Sixth and Seventh Avenues as “Barry Weinbrom Way” in honor of her father. The late Mr. Weinbrom was an active member of the Park Slope community with a passion for the environment. He was an educator teaching general sciences, environmental science, and biology in the New York City Department of Education for over thirty years. Matthew Silverman stated that Mr. Weinbrom’s interest in local environmental concerns was still relevant today. Judith Thompson commended Mr. Weinbrom for being ahead of his time.A motion was made by Judith Thompson to endorse the proposal to co-name Fifth Street between Sixth and Seventh Avenues as “Barry Weinbrom Way,” seconded by Rosemary Graham.

votes.s: Discussion of Assembly Bill A 7364-c to amend the SLA regulations for calculating the 200 foot rule and 500 foot rule measurements for proposed on premise liquor establishments.
votes.f: Discussion of Assembly Bill A 7364-c to amend the SLA regulations for calculating the 200 foot rule and 500 foot rule measurements for proposed on premise liquor establishments. The bill proposes a much stricter measurement of property line to property line (the shortest possible distance), rather than the current rule/measurement of door to door. The bill in the Assembly is now before the Economic Development Committee, while the Senate voted unanimously in favor of the bill. Also, whether an establishment can benefit from the public interest exception is now at least in part to be determined by the community board, which will be a factor. Motion to support the bill as currently written.

votes.f: Presentation made by applicant from the Clarett Group detailing why they were before the committee and asking that they be allowed to build the project as originally designed. Because of the rezoning of recent Carroll Garden, the DOB issued a Stop Work Order and the applicant must go to the BSA to have the original plans vested. They explained that 100% of the foundation is completed and that they have not continued to build is because of the current economic climate and that fully intent to complete the project once construction funds/loans are available.
